## Objective
- “Continue where you left off and finish the game.” Complete the existing 3D forest survival game into a playable game.

## Requirements
- Build request; do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Assumed the game should retain its existing 99-night survival premise and added keyboard controls and a strike action alongside the existing mobile controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Installed dependencies with `npm install`; `npm run build` succeeded before the latest source edits.
- Ran the game in Playwright and confirmed the page loaded without console errors; saved and inspected `screenshots/initial.jpg` and `screenshots/playing.jpg`.
- Added keyboard movement, strike UI/control markup, warm player lantern, strike arc, smoke/fire visuals, and HUD health ratio updates.

### Active
- Finish wiring the strike mechanic and remaining gameplay polish.
- Rebuild and test the updated game; verify gameplay and capture a latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Strike-related state and visuals were added, but there is no `attack()` implementation yet; keyboard Space and the attack button currently reference a missing function.

## Next Move
1. Implement `attack()` to strike nearby enemies in front of the player, with cooldown, damage, enemy defeat/respawn, and visible strike feedback.
2. Finish wiring attack timer, smoke animation, and night/game reset behavior; check mobile pointer input and HUD.
3. Add styling for `#attackBtn`, `#desktopHelp`, and the health panel indicator in `src/style.css`.
4. Run `npm run build`, then browser-test controls/gameplay and save/read only the latest compact JPEG.
5. Summarize assumptions and test results for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene and game logic; recent edits have left attack references unresolved.
- `src/style.css`: HUD and overlay styling; needs styling for newly added attack/help elements.

Make the character a Roblox-style blocky avatar with Roblox-like movement and camera. Keep everything else in the game as it is. Do not use any Roblox logos or names; make it an original blocky avatar.

CHARACTER LOOK:
- Blocky avatar made of 6 parts: a square head with a simple smiley face, a rectangular torso, two arms, and two legs, all boxes with slightly rounded edges.
- Classic colors: yellow skin, a colored shirt (blue), and green pants. Plastic-like, smooth material with no textures.
- Parts are separate so they can rotate and animate independently.


ANIMATIONS (like Roblox):
- Idle: the body stands still with a very subtle arm sway.
- Walk/Run: arms and legs swing back and forth in opposite pairs (left arm with right leg), the swing speed matches the movement speed. Only one move animation, no separate run.
- Jump: arms go up beside the head while rising.
- Fall: arms spread out to the sides while falling, then return to idle on landing.


MOVEMENT (Roblox feel):
- Walk speed is moderate and constant, with instant start and stop (no slow acceleration).
- Jump is a single clean jump with a floaty arc, no double jump. Hold the Jump button to keep jumping.
- The character instantly turns to face the direction it moves.
- Auto-jump over small obstacles.
- The character can climb gentle slopes and never gets stuck on edges.


CAMERA AND CONTROLS (like Roblox mobile):
- Third-person camera behind the character, slightly above.
- Left joystick: up = forward relative to the camera, down = backward, left/right = sideways. The axes must NOT be reversed.
- Drag on the right side of the screen to rotate the camera. Pinch with two fingers to zoom in and out.
- Camera collides with trees and walls so it never goes through them.
- Large Jump button on the bottom right.
- Multi-touch must work: joystick and camera at the same time.


Make sure it runs smoothly on a mid-range phone.

Add the first survival feature. Keep the Roblox-style character, the controls, and the world exactly as they are. Do not change the movement or camera.

1. CAMPFIRE: Place a campfire at the center camp with a real fire look: flames, flickering orange light, and sparks. It has a fuel level that slowly drops over time.


2. WOOD: Make some trees choppable. Add an Interact/Chop button on the right side of the screen. When the player is close to a tree and presses it, the tree shakes, then drops a wood log after a few hits. The player picks up the log by walking over it.


3. FEEDING THE FIRE: When the player is near the campfire and presses Interact while holding wood, one log is added to the fire and the fuel goes up.


4. HUD (simple and small): a wood counter at the top left and a campfire fuel bar at the top center. The bar changes color: green (strong), orange (low), red (almost out).


5. NIGHT RULE: At night, if the fire is out, the screen slowly darkens and a message says "The fire is out!". Do not add enemies yet.


Make sure the buttons are big enough for thumbs and don't overlap the joystick.

## Objective
- Finish the existing 3D forest survival game as a playable 99-night survival game.
- Fix reversed horizontal movement without changing unrelated game behavior.

## Requirements
- Retain the 99-night survival premise; support keyboard controls and a strike action alongside mobile controls.
- Forward and backward movement must remain unchanged; right/left input must move to the corresponding side of the camera, and the character must face its movement direction.
- Fix rightward camera drag only if it has the same reversal; do not change anything else.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Corrected the camera-relative right vector in `movePlayer`; camera drag already behaved correctly and was left unchanged.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented and browser-tested movement, combat, enemy response, campfire effects, HUD, night progression, and desktop/mobile controls.
- Fixed reversed horizontal movement with a one-line right-vector change in `src/main.js`.
- Verified forward/backward unchanged, left/right correct, character faces its movement direction, camera drag right looks right, no browser console errors, and `npm run build` succeeds.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. (none)

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game HUD, controls, and start overlay.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js scene, player/enemy logic, controls, combat, and night progression.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, joystick, strike button, help text, and responsive styling.
- `package.json`: Vite scripts and Three.js dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes to `index.html`, `src/main.js`, and `src/style.css` are uncommitted.
- The horizontal movement fix changes only the camera-relative right vector in `src/main.js`; camera drag was not modified.
- Night progression was verified by setting the in-game timer near its threshold rather than waiting a full night.

8. When near fire with wood, label FEED FIRE. Works.

9. Default interact near nothing -> INTERACT. Works.

10. Buttons big enough and not overlap joystick. Verified.

11. Night rule: "Do not add enemies yet." We didn't add any. Existing enemies still there. But our fire out condition doesn't remove enemies. Fine.

12. There's an issue: when fire out, `state.fireOut` stays true even if game isn't started? startGame resets false. Good.

13. Fire out message appears only if state.started. During fire out, #darkness and warning classes. Good.

14. Feeding fire while out: state.fireOut set false, but darkness CSS fades out over 4s (transition 4s). That's okay; "slowly darkens" also slowly brightens. Could use different transition for removing class? CSS same both ways. Acceptable.

15. If fuel drains to 0 and then the player dies, resetToMenu removes darkness. Good.

16. Game over existing behavior. Fine.

17. There's a potential issue in updateHud: `fireWarning.classList.toggle('visible', fireIsOut)` every frame. It doesn't restart CSS animation because class unchanged. Good.

18. On menu, fuel bar shows 100 and fire strong. fine.

19. Update loop runs updateInteractionTarget before player position updated? In animate, movePlayer first then updateInteractionTarget. Good.

20. Chopping tree sets player facing tree, and if player holds movement keys, next frame movement resets facing. That's expected.

21. Interact button pointerdown does not set pointer capture. That's fine; it's a tap. For multi-touch, works. But on mobile, if thumb drags off button maybe no issue.

22. Look zone z-index 12, buttons 19/18; darkness z13 pointer-events none. HUD z20. Joystick z15. Interact button z19. Good.

23. Joystick does not overlap.

26. "campfire fuel bar at top center" yes.

29. "When the player is close to a tree and presses it, the tree shakes, then drops a wood log after a few hits." We do 3 hits; each hit shakes. Good. But the tree doesn't visibly "drop" the log from the canopy; it pops from near base. Requirement just "drops a wood log after a few hits". Fine.

30. "The player picks up the log by walking over it." Auto-pickup within 1.15. Good.

Add these features. Keep the Roblox-style character, controls, camera, and world exactly as they are. Do not change the movement.

1. DAY/NIGHT CYCLE:
- Day lasts about 3 minutes, night about 2 minutes, with smooth sunset and sunrise.
- Show "Night X / 99" and a small sun/moon icon on the HUD.
- Night stays bright enough to see the ground (moonlight), but darker and foggier than day.


2. MONSTERS (night only):
- Low-poly shadow creatures with glowing eyes that walk on the ground with a walking animation (no floating).
- They spawn at the edge of the map when night starts and walk toward the player and the campfire.
- Night 1 has 2 monsters. Add 1 more monster each night, and make them slightly faster and stronger over time.
- A strong fire scares them: they won't come within about 6 meters of the campfire while its fuel is above half. If the fire is out, they attack freely.
- At sunrise, all monsters fade away.


3. COMBAT:
- Add an Attack button on the right side, next to Jump and Interact. The player swings an axe with a short animation and hit effect.

- If health reaches 0, show "You fell" and respawn at the camp at the start of the same night.


4. TREES AND SAPLINGS:
- When a tree is chopped down, it falls and drops 3 wood logs and 1 small sapling.
- Add a Plant button that appears when the player holds a sapling. Pressing it plants the sapling on the ground in front of the player.

This is a gameplay issue: FUEL_DRAIN_PER_SECOND 0.8, day 180s -> fire out at 125s, so at night start fire is out unless player feeds. The original game had 18s nights and 0.8 drain; with 3-minute days, fire drains too fast. The user asked for day/night cycle but likely expects fire to last. Requirement: "A strong fire scares them ... If fire is out, they attack freely." Starting with 100 fuel and no wood (player must chop) during a 3-minute day. The fire will go out before night unless fed. That may be intended survival tension, but it means at night 1 the fire is likely out and monsters attack freely, making it hard. The player can chop wood and feed, each log +25 (31s of fuel), so they need ~4-5 logs to keep fire through a 180s day + 120s night. There are only 8 closest choppable trees etc. 3 logs per tree, so feasible. But the day starts with fire 100 and drains 0.8/s; to keep it burning through day and night (300s) needs 240 fuel => ~6 logs after initial 100. Choppable trees 8 closest + every 4th (90/4≈22) plus others; enough. But a new player may not realize. The start hint says chop wood/feed. Good.

However, maybe tune fuel drain lower to account for longer cycle. The original night was 18s, so 0.8/s drained 14.4 per night. Now with 300s cycle, 0.8/s is 240 per cycle. A log gives 25 (31s). Need ~10 logs per cycle. With 3 logs per tree, 4 trees per cycle. There are plenty of trees; 22 choppable. But the game might become a wood-feeding grind. The requirement didn't specify fuel drain; "Keep ... as they are" maybe don't change. Keep 0.8. It's manageable. The day/night length change inherently affects it. We could reduce drain to 0.35 to keep similar logs per night relative. But that changes gameplay. The user said keep world/controls/camera, not fuel. Hmm.

Let's think: 99 nights with 300s each = 8.25 hours of gameplay. The fire fuel economy: each night 120s * 0.8 = 96 fuel (4 logs), plus day 180s * 0.8=144 fuel (6 logs) if maintaining fire all day. You can let it burn out during day and relight at night, saving fuel. But relighting: feedFire sets fuel +25 and fireOut false. If the fire is out during day, no health regen but monsters absent; fine. So a player can only fuel at night: 4 logs per night, chopping 2 trees. Reasonable. Starting fuel 100 covers most of day; at night start if fuel ~0, they feed. So the first night may start with fire out unless they feed. They have 3 min to gather wood; likely. Fine. No change needed.

Make the game landscape-only and add a Roblox-style hotbar with an Axe and a Backpack, plus a new item-carrying system. Keep the character, world, day/night, and monsters unchanged.

LANDSCAPE:
- Lock to landscape (screen.orientation.lock in fullscreen). In portrait show a full-screen "Rotate your phone" message and pause the game.
- Layout: joystick at bottom left, action buttons in an arc at bottom right (Jump, Interact, Drop), hotbar at bottom center, HUD (health, hunger, counters, night counter, fuel bar) along the top. Nothing overlaps. Respect safe areas. Right-half drag rotates the camera.


HOTBAR (Roblox style):
- A row of small rounded squares at the bottom center, each with a clear icon, and a small number in its corner.
- Slot 1: Axe icon. Slot 2: Backpack icon. Empty slots stay hidden.
- Tapping a slot equips that tool and it appears in the character's right hand. The equipped slot is clearly marked: a bright white border, a slight glow, and the square raised and scaled up a little; the others are dimmed.
- Tapping the equipped slot again unequips it and the hand becomes empty.
- Only one tool is equipped at a time, with a short equip animation.
- The Attack/Chop button appears only when the Axe is equipped.
- The Backpack slot shows an item counter badge (for example 4/20).


NO AUTO-PICKUP:
- Items (wood logs, saplings, berries) are no longer collected by walking near them. They stay on the ground.


CARRYING ITEMS:
- When the player is near an item and taps it (or presses Interact), the item lifts and floats just above the ground, then follows the player smoothly. The player can drag up to 3 items this way.
- If the Backpack is equipped when the player taps an item, the item goes straight into the backpack (capacity 20) with a small pop animation, and the counter updates.
- The Backpack in the character's hand looks the same as the backpack model in the world: a small blocky brown bag with a flap and straps.
- Add a Drop button: dropping releases the floating items to the ground. Dropping a backpack item takes it out in front of the player.
- Tapping the equipped Backpack again opens a simple inventory panel showing the stored items with counts, with a close button.
- Floating items near the campfire can be thrown in with Interact to add fuel. Backpack items can be taken out from the inventory panel.


Make all buttons thumb-sized, semi-transparent, and smooth on a mid-range phone.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Update the existing forest survival game with landscape-only mobile controls and a Roblox-style hotbar/inventory item-carrying system.
- Preserve the existing character, world, day/night cycle, monsters, and movement.

## Requirements
- Lock to landscape in fullscreen; in portrait, show a full-screen “Rotate your phone” message and pause the game.
- Landscape layout: joystick bottom-left, thumb-sized action buttons in an arc bottom-right (Jump, Interact, Drop), hotbar bottom-center, and health, hunger, counters, night counter, and fuel bar along the top; avoid overlap and respect safe areas.
- Right-half screen drag rotates the camera.
- Add a Roblox-style hotbar with Axe in slot 1 and Backpack in slot 2; hide empty slots. Tapping equips/unequips a tool, shows it in the character’s right hand, and uses a short equip animation. Mark the selected slot with a bright border, glow, lift, and scale. Show Attack/Chop only when the Axe is equipped.
- Show a Backpack item counter badge (e.g. `4/20`); tapping the equipped Backpack again opens an inventory panel with counts and a close button.
- Do not auto-pickup logs, saplings, or berries. Nearby items can be tapped or collected with Interact to float and follow the player; carry up to 3 this way. With Backpack equipped, collect directly into its 20-item capacity with a pop animation.
- Backpack hand/world models should match: a small blocky brown bag with flap and straps.
- Drop releases carried floating items; dropping an inventory item places it in front of the player. Interact can throw floating items near the campfire in as fuel. Inventory panel supports taking items out.
- Buttons should be thumb-sized, semi-transparent, and smooth on mid-range phones.

## Decisions
- The previous feature implementation assumed planted saplings grow into choppable trees after 45 seconds; the original planting prompt ended mid-sentence.
- Existing camera-relative movement correction and camera drag behavior were previously tested; movement should remain unchanged.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing day/night, monsters, combat/health/respawn, and tree/log/sapling features are implemented and previously browser-tested; `npm run build` and production smoke test passed.
- Reviewed the current `index.html`, `src/main.js`, and `src/style.css` while beginning the new task.

### Active
- Implement landscape lock/portrait pause overlay and reorganize touch controls/HUD.
- Implement hotbar equipment visuals and Axe/Backpack hand models.
- Replace automatic item pickup with carry, backpack storage, dropping, fire feeding, and inventory interactions.
- Validate on mobile-sized landscape and portrait viewports while preserving the existing game behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant sections of `index.html`, `src/main.js`, and `src/style.css`, especially input handlers, item update loops, HUD updates, and existing mobile controls.
2. Implement the landscape/portrait behavior and responsive HUD/control layout.
3. Add hotbar/equipment state and models, then refactor item pickup/storage/drop/fire-feeding paths.
4. Run `node --check src/main.js`, `npm run build`, and browser checks for portrait pause, landscape layout, item flows, and regressions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current HUD and touch-control markup; update for hotbar, inventory panel, drop button, and rotation overlay.
- `src/main.js`: Game state, controls, interaction, item updates, models, and HUD logic.
- `src/style.css`: HUD, controls, responsive layout, and touch-target styling.
- `capture.mjs`: Modified in the working tree; inspect before changing or overwriting.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. The current working tree also contains generated `dist/` changes from builds; do not assume they are source changes.
- A previous browser run reported 35/35 checks, including zero page/console errors, but those checks predate the new hotbar and carrying requirements.

"Make the game landscape-only and add a Roblox-style hotbar with an Axe and a Backpack, plus a new item-carrying system. Keep the character, world, day/night, and monsters unchanged.

LANDSCAPE:
- Lock to landscape (screen.orientation.lock in fullscreen). In portrait show a full-screen \"Rotate your phone\" message and pause the game.
- Layout: joystick at bottom left, action buttons in an arc at bottom right (Jump, Interact, Drop), hotbar at bottom center, HUD (health, hunger, counters, night counter, fuel bar) along the top. Nothing overlaps. Respect safe areas. Right-half drag rotates the camera.

HOTBAR (Roblox style):
- A row of small rounded squares at the bottom center, each with a clear icon, and a small number in its corner.
- Slot 1: Axe icon. Slot 2: Backpack icon. Empty slots stay hidden.
- Tapping a slot equips that tool and it appears in the character's right hand. The equipped slot is clearly marked: a bright white border, a slight glow, and the square raised and scaled up a little; the others are dimmed.
- Tapping the equipped slot again unequips it and the hand becomes empty.
- Only one tool is equipped at a time, with a short equip animation.
- The Attack/Chop button appears only when the Axe is equipped.
- The Backpack slot shows an item counter badge (for example 4/20).

NO AUTO-PICKUP:
- Items (wood logs, saplings, berries) are no longer collected by walking near them. They stay on the ground.

CARRYING ITEMS:
- When the player is near an item and taps it (or presses Interact), the item lifts and floats just above the ground, then follows the player smoothly. The player can drag up to 3 items this way.
- If the Backpack is equipped when the player taps an item, the item goes straight into the backpack (capacity 20) with a small pop animation, and the counter updates.
- The Backpack in the character's hand looks the same as the backpack model in the world: a small blocky brown bag with a flap and straps.
- Add a Drop button: dropping releases the floating items to the ground. Dropping a backpack item takes it out in front of the player.
- Tapping the equipped Backpack again opens a simple inventory panel showing the stored items with counts, with a close button.
- Floating items near the campfire can be thrown in with Interact to add fuel. Backpack items can be taken out from the inventory panel.

Make all buttons thumb-sized, semi-transparent, and smooth on a mid-range phone."

- Update the existing forest survival game with landscape-only mobile controls and a Roblox-style hotbar/inventory item-carrying system while preserving the existing game and movement.

- Lock to landscape in fullscreen; in portrait, show a “Rotate your phone” overlay and pause the game.

- Avoid automatic pickup of logs, saplings, and berries; support carrying up to 3, Backpack storage up to 20, dropping, inventory take-out, and campfire feeding.
- Backpack hand/world models should match as a blocky brown bag with flap and straps.

- Planted saplings grow into choppable trees after 45 seconds.
- Preserve the existing camera-relative movement and camera drag behavior.

Add an Upgrade Machine, iron, and sound. Keep everything else unchanged, including the Roblox-style character, landscape controls, hotbar, backpack, and monsters. If a workbench or crafting panel already exists, replace it with this machine.

UPGRADE MACHINE:
- Place a blocky metal machine near the campfire: a wooden hopper on top, a small chimney, and a glowing front panel. It puffs smoke and glows orange while working.
- Interact with it to open a panel (landscape layout, big buttons). The player feeds it wood from the backpack or floating items, which fills a "Fuel" bar.
- Upgrades cost wood and iron, take about 10 seconds with a progress bar, then appear in front of the machine to collect:
  - Iron Axe: 6 wood + 3 iron (chops faster, hits harder).
  - Pickaxe: 4 wood + 1 iron (needed to mine iron).
  - Iron Sword: 5 wood + 5 iron (strong melee).
  - Iron Wall: 8 wood + 6 iron (sturdy wall placed near the campfire).
  - Bigger Campfire: 10 wood + 5 iron (larger light and scare radius).
- The machine stops without fuel. Show a clear message if materials are missing.


IRON:
- Add gray rocks with orange-brown streaks in rocky areas and at the forest edge.
- With the Pickaxe equipped, tapping a rock cracks it and drops 2-3 iron pieces that go into the backpack or float to the player like other items. Rocks regrow after a while.
- Iron has its own icon and counter in the backpack.
- All new tools appear in the hotbar.


SOUND (Web Audio API with generated sounds only, no external files):
- Ambient loop: wind and crickets at night, birds and soft wind by day, switching smoothly with the day/night cycle.
- Campfire crackling that is louder when near and quieter when far.
- Footsteps matching the walk speed, plus jump and landing sounds.
- Axe whoosh, tree thud, tree falling crash, and metallic clink on rocks.
- Machine hum and clanking while working, with a "ding" when an item is ready.
- Monster growls and footsteps that get louder when close, and a heartbeat that speeds up when a monster is near.
- Pickup pop, equip click, a cheerful chime for "Child saved!", and a sad tone when the player falls.
- A mute button in a top corner and a volume slider in a simple settings panel.
- Start audio after the first touch, since mobile browsers block autoplay.


Make it run smoothly on a mid-range phone.

Now design implementation in detail.

We need to modify big main.js. Let's plan carefully.

### Data model

New item type: `iron`. Add:
- state.backpack { wood, sapling, berry, iron }
- totals/capacity includes iron.
- ITEM_NAMES iron: 'Iron piece'
- backpackCount includes iron.
- makeGroundItemMesh iron mesh (small gray chunk with orange streak).
- inventory row iron, icon CSS.
- hotbar new tool slots: pickaxe, ironAxe, ironSword, ironWall maybe? Requirement "All new tools appear in the hotbar." Upgrade outputs: Iron Axe, Pickaxe, Iron Sword, Iron Wall, Bigger Campfire. Tools: iron axe, pickaxe, iron sword; wall and bigger campfire are placed automatically? "Iron Wall ... sturdy wall placed near the campfire" and "Bigger Campfire ... larger light and scare radius". These appear in front of the machine to collect, then maybe when collected they auto-place? Hmm.

"Upgrades cost wood and iron, take about 10 seconds with a progress bar, then appear in front of the machine to collect" — all 5 upgrades appear as ground items. "Iron Wall (sturdy wall placed near the campfire)" and "Bigger Campfire (larger light and scare radius)" could be collected and then placed automatically near the campfire on pickup. Or the player carries them and uses them. Simpler: collect the item; when picked up, iron wall is placed near campfire and bigger campfire applies upgrade. But "All new tools appear in the hotbar" likely means iron axe, pickaxe, iron sword (and maybe wall?). "New tools" = tools. Maybe add hotbar slots for Pickaxe, Iron Axe, Iron Sword. Wall and bigger campfire are upgrades not tools. That satisfies.

But then hotbar could have 5 slots: Axe, Pickaxe, Iron Axe, Iron Sword, Backpack. On mobile, hotbar gets wide. Need compact sizes. Roblox-style hotbar: slot 1 axe, 2 pickaxe, 3 iron axe, 4 iron sword, 5 backpack. We should hide locked slots until owned to save width. But "All new tools appear in the hotbar" — show slots when crafted/collected. Start with Axe and Backpack. When pickaxe/iron axe/iron sword crafted, slots appear. Good.

Could also show slot for wall? No, not a tool.

State: `state.tools = { axe: true, pickaxe: false, ironAxe: false, ironSword: false }` (or `ownedTools`). Equipped tool can be those + backpack. Starting axe owned. Pickaxe/iron axe/iron sword enabled after collection.

Upgrade definitions:
```
const UPGRADES = {
  ironAxe: { name:'Iron Axe', cost:{wood:6, iron:3}, time:10, kind:'tool' },
  pickaxe: { name:'Pickaxe', cost:{wood:4, iron:1}, ... },
  ironSword: { name:'Iron Sword', cost:{wood:5, iron:5} },
  ironWall: { name:'Iron Wall', cost:{wood:8, iron:6} },
  biggerCampfire: { name:'Bigger Campfire', cost:{wood:10, iron:5} },
}
```

Machine:
- position near campfire, e.g. x=3.2, z=-2.6? Need open space, avoid player spawn (0,-3.5), campfire center. Let's place at (3.6, 0, -1.6) maybe. Campfire radius 1.5. Machine near. Need avoid tree spawn? Trees radius >=12, fine. Berry radius >=8.5. Player at z=-3.5; machine at (3.5,-2.0) is 3.5 away. Fine.
- Build model: group, metal gray body, wooden hopper on top (cone/frustum), chimney, glowing panel (emissive box). Add PointLight orange inside.
- Smoke puffs, working animation.
- Add to scene at ground height.
- `machine.position.set(MACHINE_X, groundH, MACHINE_Z)`.
- interact range 2.8.
- state.machine: `{ fuel: 0, working: null?, progress: 0, ready: []? }`.

Machine behavior:
- Interact opens panel. Panel HTML: overlay/panel anchored center? Landscape layout big buttons. Needs handle while game behind; pause? Probably keep game running but panel open. To avoid monsters killing while panel open? Could pause? User says "Interact with it to open a panel". We'll allow game continued, but panel blocks pointer. Simplicity: state.machineOpen; opening hides toast and inventory; look input disabled while panel open? Right half drag currently blocked only by inventoryOpen. Add machineOpen.

- Feeding: "The player feeds it wood from the backpack or floating items, which fills a 'Fuel' bar."
  - In panel: a "ADD WOOD" button consumes one wood from backpack and adds e.g. 25 fuel (max 100). Maybe also iron? No.
  - "floating items" means ground items? In 3D, when near machine with carried items (floating/carried) and pushing interact could feed. Or panel can have "Load carried wood" button that consumes carried wood items and adds fuel. Could also allow tapping wood items? Since machine panel open, world taps blocked. Provide "ADD WOOD" that uses backpack wood, and "USE HELD WOOD" maybe. Simpler: "Feed Wood" button consumes wood from backpack if available, else carried wood items if present. That covers both.
  - Each wood adds 25 fuel. Fuel drains while working (e.g., 100 fuel for a full 10s upgrade? Use 0.9/sec? 10s * maybe 4/sec = 40). Let's make fuel 0-100, drain 3.5/sec while working → 35 per upgrade. One wood = 20? Let's set wood fuel 25. 2 wood basically enough. Clear.
  - Actually user says "which fills a 'Fuel' bar" — display fuel bar in panel and maybe HUD? Only panel.
  - Machine stops without fuel: progress pauses, message "Out of fuel" and sound stops. It continues when fuel added.

- Upgrade selection: five big buttons with costs, disabled if insufficient? Better allow click and show message if missing. If machine working, ignore. If ready item pending, maybe allow queue? Simpler: only one at a time; completed item spawns in front. If machine idle and ready item not collected, can start another? "then appear in front of the machine to collect" immediately upon completion. So ready item is a world item. Player can start next. But machine slot output floating item; no queue.

- On start: deduct materials, set working upgrade, progress 0, fuel remains. Play machine start.
- Each frame while working: if fuel>0 drain, progress += delta; glow orange, puff smoke. If fuel hits 0, pause with status message once.
- On complete: spawn output item in front; play ding; show toast; machine returns idle; maybe cooldown 0.6.
  - Tools appear as ground "upgrade item" that when picked up unlock tool. Need interaction: `pickUpItem` handles new types. For tool upgrade items, pickup should add to ownedTools not backpack. Maybe show ground item with icon-ish 3D mesh. When near, interact label "COLLECT IRON AXE". Floating to player like other items? Could reuse groundItems with type 'ironAxe' etc, and `pickUpItem` special. However backpack limits etc: tools aren't inventory items. We can let pickup apply only when near (PICKUP_RANGE). Add to `groundItems` types with `custom` flag? Let's generalize.

Item type list currently wood/sapling/berry. Add iron + upgrade types: `pickaxe`, `ironAxe`, `ironSword`, `ironWall`, `biggerCampfire`.
- `makeGroundItemMesh` create 3D meshes:
  - iron: small gray rock chunk with orange streak.
  - pickaxe: handle + gray head.
  - ironAxe: iron axe model (bigger).
  - ironSword: sword model.
  - ironWall: wall segment model.
  - biggerCampfire: perhaps a coiled log ring / upgrade token.
- `pickUpItem`: if type is tool upgrade:
  - for pickaxe/ironAxe/ironSword: unlock tool (`state.tools[type] = true`), remove ground item, show toast, update hotbar UI. Should not go to backpack.
  - for ironWall: place wall near campfire, remove item.
  - biggerCampfire: apply upgrade: increase fire light and scare radius, maybe visual scale of campfire base/flame; remove item.
- "go into the backpack or float to the player like other items" for iron: existing pickUp logic: if backpack equipped -> backpack; else carried. Fine. Iron can be carried too (max 3). Need fuel? Machine feeding iron? no.
- Iron rocks: new array `ironRocks` with mesh, hits, cracked, regrow. Add 8-10 at rocky areas / forest edge. Need integrated target detection for pickaxe. Add `state.targetRock`. updateInteractionTarget should select nearest choppable tree OR iron rock based on equipped tool? Prompt:
  - if pickaxe equipped && targetRock -> "MINE IRON"
  - if axe/ironAxe/ironSword && targetTree -> "CHOP" (sword maybe not chop? User says Iron Axe chops faster, hits harder; sword strong melee. Let's allow axe and iron axe to chop, sword only attack; pickaxe mines).
- Attack button: visible when tool is axe/ironAxe/ironSword/pickaxe? Requirement "If the Pickaxe equipped, tapping a rock cracks it". Attack button shows for melee tools. Label MINE when pickaxe + target rock, CHOP when axe/iron axe + target tree, ATTACK otherwise. If pickaxe equipped and not rock, ATTACK maybe no damage? It's a tool; could attack weakly. Let's do pickaxe damage 1.
- Attack function currently returns if tool !== axe. Generalize `isMeleeTool`, `isChoppingTool`, `isMiningTool`.
  - Iron axe: chops faster (attack cooldown lower), hits harder (damage 2, tree damage maybe 2 hits). Base axe has hits 3, attackCooldown .58, damage 1.
  - Iron Sword: strong melee (damage maybe 3, cooldown .45), no tree chop.
  - Pickaxe: mining rock only, maybe damage 1.
- tree hits: `chopTree(tree, power)` reduce hits by power. Iron axe power 2 maybe; tree falls in 2 hits. Also chop animation timing.
- Rocks: each rock hits 2 (or 3). Each hit cracks it visually (scale down slightly, emissive flash, particle). On break: drop 2-3 iron items + maybe stone? Requirement only iron. Then hide rock; regrow after e.g. 30-45s; reset. Each tap attack? "tapping a rock cracks it and drops 2-3 iron pieces" could mean one tap; but crack stages suggest multiple hits. We'll do 2 taps; on break drops 2-3. Prompt "MINE". Maybe one tap if iron pickaxe? No.

- Rock target in updateInteractionTarget: nearest rock within TREE_INTERACT_RANGE when pickaxe equipped (or always but prompt only when pickaxe).
- Interact button can mine when pickaxe targetRock, same as attack. The user says tapping a rock. Attack button visible. Also tapping directly on rock via world tap should mine? Requirement says "tapping a rock". Our world tap currently picks up items. We can add raycast for rocks/trees/machine: if tap rock and pickaxe equipped and within range, mine; if tap tree with axe, chop; if tap machine, open panel. That makes direct tapping work. But ensure attack button also works.
- Add rock meshes to tap candidates. Similar machine. Need efficient.
- Interaction priority: machine near? If near machine, maybe INTERACT opens panel. But currently fire/tree/item priorities. Add machine before fire? The machine is near campfire, so player standing between both. If near machine, `INTERACT` should open machine. But then feeding fire becomes harder because machine is within its range at 2.6. Could set machine interact range 2.4 and fire range 3.8; if player near machine but also fire, machine wins. Maybe prompt order: nearby item first; then machine if in reach (label "UPGRADE"); then tree chop; then fire. But if player wants fire, they'd step away? Machine at 3.6 from fire; FIRE_FEED_RANGE 3.8, so there's overlap. Could place machine at (4.4, -2.4), distance ~5 from fire, range 2.4. Then most fire interactions still accessible but less overlap. Campfire influence radius 7. Let's compute: machine at (4.2, -3.0) distance 5.16 from fire. Fire feed range 3.8, machine range 2.5; overlap region possible but limited. Fine.
  - Also machine uses floating items: when standing near with carried wood and interacting, maybe load wood into machine. But if machine opens panel, we feed via button. That's fine. Maybe interact prompt "USE MACHINE".

- Upgrade panel UI:
  - Markup: fixed panel maybe centered right-ish; aesthetic.
  - Header "UPGRADE MACHINE", close.
  - Fuel row with bar and percentage; "ADD WOOD (1)" button.
  - status line text.
  - progress bar row shown when working; label upgrade + remaining secs.
  - list of upgrade buttons each with name, cost, time; "CRAFT" maybe card. Big buttons min-height 44.
  - Should fit landscape small heights (~390px). Need scrollable list with 5 rows; 5*44=220 + header/fuel ~110 => 330. Fine. On max-height 350, compact. We'll make panel width min(560px, 92vw) and max-height calc(100vh - 20px), with scroll list. Maybe use grid 2 columns on wider? For 844x390, 2 columns of cards using CSS grid would fit nicely, each 160px wide. "big buttons" yes. Let's do `.upgrade-grid` 2 columns. Each card button has name, cost, description maybe. Height ~70. 3 rows = 230 + header ~100 => 330. Fine, scroll.
  - Keep touch targets >=44.

- Item icons: add iron to counter row? Requirement "Iron has its own icon and counter in the backpack." So inventory row is enough, maybe HUD counter too? It says "in the backpack". We'll add HUD counter to stats panel? The stats row has wood/sap/berry; adding iron would crowd but can add. Requirement icon and counter in the backpack — inventory row does that. But also HUD helpful. Could add `IRON` counter. Maybe compact. Let's add a fourth counter with dot iron. At 844 width stats panel 154 min; 4 counters might fit with small text. At 390 width stats panel 132; labels hidden under 350. It'll fit. Good.
- Hotbar icons: need SVG for pickaxe, iron axe, iron sword. Add slots hidden initially. Use `hidden` class on hotbar-slot. When tool unlocked, show. Backpack slot remains. Slots order: Axe (1), Pickaxe (2), Iron Axe (3), Iron Sword (4), Backpack (5). But number badges. Requirement said hotbar. Update keyboard keys 1-5 accordingly. Current key 2 backpack. Changing key mapping may be okay; but "Keep ... hotbar unchanged" means preserve behavior? Better keep axe=1, backpack=2, and new tools 3/4/5. But visually order could be axe, backpack, pickaxe, iron axe, sword. Roblox hotbar typically 1-5. We can keep axe 1, backpack 2, new tools 3-5. That preserves existing key mapping. Hmm "Keep everything else unchanged, including ... hotbar" means don't break existing. Keeping 1/2 is safest. Order: Axe, Backpack, Pickaxe, Iron Axe, Iron Sword. New slots appear after backpack. However hotbar width grows; 5 slots = 5*54+4*10+12 = ~322px. On 390x844 landscape, center hotbar could overlap joystick/actions? Joystick left 118, hotbar 322 centered => left 261, right 583; action cluster right 164 => starts 673. Fine at 844. At 780 maybe. If 5*48+32+10=282, center left=249. Fine. Ensure no overlap at 640x360: hotbar 5*44+4*8+10=252; left=194, right=446; joystick 104 at left 9, action 150 at right 7 -> fine. Good.
- `updateToolUi`: equipped state for all slots; attack button visible for melee/mining tools; attack label.
- `equipTool` only allow if owned tool. If not owned, toast.
- `updateToolModels`: show correct held model. Need create new 3D models:
  - pickaxe group
  - ironAxe group
  - ironSword group
  - Held in rightArm like axe. The existing `axe` is a group. We'll create `pickaxe`, `ironAxe`, `ironSword` with similar proportions. Add to rightArm, invisible.
  - Lantern visible when no tool.
  - `handBackpack` remains.
  - `updateEquippedTool` scale/position should apply to current model. Existing AXE_BASE_Y, BACKPACK_BASE_Y. Need per-tool base Y. Store base y on each group userData.
  - `updateToolModels` toggles.
  - Avatar attack animation uses same swing; fine. For sword maybe different but okay.
  - Iron axe model: dark iron head with orange-ish glint.
  - Pickaxe: T-shape head.
  - Iron sword: long blade.

- `ownedTools` initial: { axe: true, pickaxe:false, ironAxe:false, ironSword:false }. state.ownedTools to reset each game.
- On tool unlock update hotbar visibility and maybe auto-equip? Could show toast "Iron Axe collected - press slot 3". Maybe auto-equip newly collected tool? Nice: equip automatically. But if auto-equipping, `equipTool` animates. Let's call `unlockTool(type)` sets owned, shows slot, then `equipTool(type)` after small. Simpler immediately equip. Good.
- ironWall: place near campfire. Where? Choose position relative to machine or campfire. Add wall group 3 segments maybe; sturdy. It should block enemies? Requirement "sturdy wall placed near the campfire." Implement physical wall as scene mesh and collision for enemies? "sturdy wall" suggests blocks monster path. We can add it as obstacle to enemies: if wall placed, push enemies out of wall area? That's extra. At minimum visual wall near campfire. To make it meaningful, maybe enemies collide with wall (simple AABB circle). Could add `placedWalls` array with x,z,width,depth,rotation. In updateEnemies, after movement, resolve wall collision if enemy near. Also player collision? Could annoy. Implement enemy collision only (wall protects). Maybe health? "sturdy" no destruction requested, so permanent per run. Place near campfire at fixed spot depending on count, e.g., ring at angle. Add 1 wall per craft. Good.
- biggerCampfire: increase `state.fireRadiusBonus` or `state.fireLevel`. Modify FIRE_SCARE_RADIUS usage to `getFireScareRadius()` = FIRE_SCARE_RADIUS + state.fireUpgradeLevel*2.5. Also fire glow distance/intensity and warm light distance/range, maybe increase campfire base scale and flame size. Use `state.fireUpgrade = 0` then +=1. Cap maybe 2? Could craft multiple; make each bigger: radius +2, light range +4. On collect, apply visual scale? We can scale `campfire.scale` slightly? Scaling group scales base and flame; fireGlow distances unaffected by scale but we can set. Scaling entire campfire includes y position of fire? Group scale around origin, base bottom stays at 0. Fine. `campfire.scale.setScalar(1 + 0.15*bonus)` could enlarge. But base becomes larger and might overlap player. Fine. Also update `state.fireScareRadius`.
  - `FIRE_SCARE_RADIUS` constant used in updateEnemies; replace with `getFireScareRadius()`.
  - Campfire light distances: `fireGlow.distance`, `warmLight.distance` set at creation; can update on upgrade. `fireGlow.distance = 15 + bonus*5`, warmLight.distance = 20+... Also `getCampfireInfluence` uses fixed 7 radius; maybe use 7 + bonus*1.5 so bigger fire safe zone. Good.
  - Fire "fuel" bigger? Not requested. Could cap remain.

- Machine fuel from floating items: Since groundItems include type iron/tool etc. Feeding machine should accept only wood (and maybe saplings?) Requirement "feeds it wood". Use wood only. In panel, button "ADD WOOD" consumes backpack wood first, else carried wood. If none, message. Also perhaps a button "GATHER WOOD" not needed.
- Could allow interacting with machine while carrying wood: `interact()` if near machine -> open panel (not auto-feed).
- Fuel drain only while working. Machine fuel stays when idle.

- Machine smoke: create smoke puffs group. While working, puffs rise and opacity increases. Use 5 puffs; update function.
- Glowing front panel: emissive material intensity animate; orange point light; while working more intense. Idle dim glow.
- Machine hum audio while working, clanking. Audio handled in audio system with loop/oscillator; start/stop.

### Audio

Implement a full `audio` module inside main.js. Must start after first touch. Use AudioContext.

Architecture:
- `const audio = { ctx: null, master: null, muted:false, volume: 0.7, started:false, ... }`
- `initAudio()` called on first pointerdown/keydown/click; create AudioContext, master gain -> destination; create noise buffer(s) for reuse (2s white noise); start ambient system.
- Mute button toggles `muted`, sets master gain 0 or volume.
- slider sets volume.
- Avoid expensive per-frame node creation. Use stable loops.

Ambient:
  - Wind: looping noise buffer source through lowpass filter; gain modulated with day factor. Day: gain 0.035; night: 0.02.
  - Crickets at night: create oscillator? Better noise + bandpass high-frequency with amplitude modulation. Could use 3 sine oscillators around 4200-4800 Hz with LFO gain; only audible at night. Maybe create buffer noise loop through bandpass 4500Hz and gain modulated by slow LFO. Use one looping noise -> bandpass(4200) -> gain with ripple. We can use oscillator LFO -> gain.gain.
  - Birds by day: schedule chirps at random intervals via setTimeout? Avoid timers? Web audio scheduling inside main update loop is better. In `updateAudio(delta)`, manage timers using accumulators; when day and random, playBirdChirp(). Same for wind gusts.
  - Smooth switch: ambient gains lerp toward target based on daylight in updateAudio.
  - Implement wind via noise source -> lowpass 500 -> gain `windGain`.
  - Cricket via noise source -> bandpass 3800 Q 8 -> gain `cricketGain`, plus LFO tremolo.
  - During day, birds scheduled every 4-9s, 3 quick chirps with oscillator frequency ramps.
  - Soft wind by day: gain slightly higher.

- Campfire crackling: create noise source -> bandpass (800) -> gain; plus random crackle pops scheduled based on proximity and fire burning. Distance-based gain. Could use a looping noise with filter + amplitude modulation; and random short noise bursts (crackle) using `playCrackle()` each ~0.1-0.4s depending on distance. Need avoid too many nodes; 3-6 per second okay. Use shared noise buffer and short source/biquad/gain envelope. distance attenuation: gain = clamp(1 - dist/18). Intensity higher when near.
  - Could just use one looping filtered noise with gain based on distance and random crackle bursts.

- Footsteps matching walk speed: in update, if moveSpeed>0 and grounded, accumulate step timer interval = maybe 0.32 / (moveSpeed/6) → 0.32s. Play soft filtered noise thump with pitch variation. Jump sound when tryJump; landing when grounded transition.
  - Need detect landing: in updatePlayerVertical when landing, if velocityY < -3 call audio.land().
  - Footstep sounds only when started and not paused.
  - avoid audio in menu.

- Axe whoosh: on attack/chop, play noise sweep (bandpass with freq ramp) + tree thud on tree hit; tree falling crash when fellTree; rock metallic clink on rock hit.
- Machine hum + clanking while working: use oscillator sawtooth low freq (60-90 Hz) through lowpass + gain, start when working, stop when not; clank scheduled ~0.5s with metallic ping/noise.
- ding when item ready.
- Monster growls/footsteps louder when close: in updateAudio, find nearest enemy distance; schedule growl every 3-7s scaled; footsteps from nearest enemy every 0.5s when moving, gain distance. Heartbeat: schedule two-thump at interval mapped from distance (when within ~14). Use oscillator low freq sine with short envelope; interval from 1.1s far to 0.4s near. Need "speeds up when monster is near". Manage `heartTimer`; when no enemies near, no heartbeat. Use nearest visible enemy. Also growl sounds.
- pickup pop, equip click, cheerful chime for "Child saved!", sad tone when player falls.
  - pickup: `playPickup()` in pickUpItem/addItemToBackpack/take? Add to pickUpItem and addItem.
  - equip click in equipTool.
  - child saved: Hook where? Let's inspect game win at 99 nights; maybe "Child saved!" when surviving a night? Could trigger on dawn/regrowBerries? Hmm. The requirement might just be a sound event expected. We can implement `playChildSaved()` and trigger at `state.night` increment (each dawn) with toast "Child saved!"? But no child. Maybe in this game "children" are not implemented. Could add a chime at dawn and toast "A new day survives"? But user explicitly says cheerful chime for "Child saved!". Could add a rare event: at dawn, if fire survived and nightActive, show "Child saved!" toast and chime. That would fit survival theme (saving children from night). It's a change to game feedback but not a major mechanic. Alternatively trigger on victory ("You Survived") and keep text. But less likely to hear.
  - Maybe add a child NPC at camp? That's much bigger and user said keep everything else unchanged. Don't.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add an Upgrade Machine, iron gathering and crafting, and generated Web Audio sounds to the existing forest survival game.
- Preserve the existing character, world, monsters, landscape controls, hotbar, backpack, and gameplay.

## Requirements
- Place a blocky metal Upgrade Machine near the campfire, with a wooden hopper, chimney, glowing front panel, smoke, and orange glow while working.
- Let players interact with the machine, add wood from the backpack or nearby floating items as fuel, and show a fuel bar and clear missing-material messages.
- Craft five upgrades with the specified costs and roughly 10-second progress: Iron Axe (6 wood, 3 iron), Pickaxe (4 wood, 1 iron), Iron Sword (5 wood, 5 iron), Iron Wall (8 wood, 6 iron), and Bigger Campfire (10 wood, 5 iron); completed items appear in front of the machine to collect.
- Add iron-bearing rocks in rocky areas and at the forest edge; a Pickaxe cracks them and yields 2–3 iron, and rocks regrow after a delay.
- Show iron with its own icon and backpack counter; add new tools to the hotbar.
- Generate all requested ambient, interaction, monster, and player sounds with Web Audio API only; add mute and volume controls, and start audio after first touch.
- Keep performance suitable for a mid-range phone.

## Decisions
- No new implementation decisions recorded.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing landscape-only game controls, character/world, hotbar, backpack, and monster systems are implemented.
- Inspected relevant game systems and searched for rescue/child-save references; no such feature was found.

### Active
- Implement the machine, iron resource and upgrades, and generated audio while preserving existing gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining relevant UI, interaction, and animation code, then implement the requested features and integrate them with existing systems.
2. Run syntax/build checks and test the new interactions, audio controls, and performance without regressing existing mobile gameplay.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game state, world interactions, crafting/resource logic, enemies, and animation.
- `index.html`: HUD and UI markup for machine, inventory, and audio controls.
- `src/style.css`: Landscape HUD and responsive mobile layouts.
- `dist/`: Generated production build; currently reflects modified build output.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. A prior status showed `src/main.js`, `src/style.css`, `index.html`, `dist/`, `start.sh`, `capture.mjs`, and `capture.sh` modified or changed; `capture.mjs` and `capture.sh` may be user work and should be inspected before editing.
- Existing backpack resources are `wood`, `sapling`, and `berry`; add iron consistently with current inventory and hotbar patterns.
- Existing campfire fuel drains in `updateCampfire(delta)`; machine fuel should be separate from campfire fuel.

## Objective
- Add an Upgrade Machine, iron gathering and crafting, and generated Web Audio sounds to the forest survival game while preserving existing gameplay and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Place a blocky metal Upgrade Machine near the campfire with a wooden hopper, chimney, glowing front panel, smoke, and an orange glow while working.
- Let players add wood from their backpack or nearby items as separate machine fuel; show a fuel bar and clear missing-material messages.
- Craft Iron Axe (6 wood, 3 iron), Pickaxe (4 wood, 1 iron), Iron Sword (5 wood, 5 iron), Iron Wall (8 wood, 6 iron), and Bigger Campfire (10 wood, 5 iron), with about 10 seconds of progress; output items appear in front of the machine to collect.
- Add iron-bearing rocks in rocky areas and at the forest edge; a Pickaxe cracks them for 2–3 iron, and rocks regrow after a delay.
- Show iron in the backpack and HUD; add crafted tools to the hotbar.
- Generate ambient, interaction, monster, and player sounds with Web Audio API only; provide mute and volume controls; start audio after first touch.
- Preserve the existing character, world, monsters, landscape controls, hotbar, backpack, and gameplay; keep performance suitable for a mid-range phone.

## Decisions
- Machine fuel is separate from campfire fuel.
- Implemented iron rocks with two hits, 2–3 iron drops, and randomized 28–44 second regrowth.
- Machine consumes fuel while an upgrade is active and pauses if it runs out.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added machine model, fuel/job panel, upgrade options, crafting progress, and collectible upgrade outputs.
- Added iron rocks and pickups, iron backpack/HUD display, Pickaxe mining, tool hotbar slots/models, and iron crafting item collection.
- Added Iron Wall placement and Bigger Campfire scaling/light/safety-radius effects.
- Added procedural Web Audio sounds, ambient loops, mute, volume controls, and first-interaction audio initialization.
- `node --check src/main.js` and `npm run build` succeeded before the latest machine position/CSS tweaks.
- Browser tests exercised machine fueling, crafting, out-of-fuel pause/resume, iron mining and regrowth, item collection, structures, audio controls, and hotbar visibility; no browser errors were reported.

### Active
- Review and finish browser QA, address any issues found, then rebuild `dist/` after the latest source changes.
- Preserve existing uncommitted/user changes while inspecting and verifying.

### Blocked

1. Run syntax checks and `npm run build` after the latest changes; verify generated `dist/` files are consistent.
2. Inspect mobile screenshots and test interaction flows, especially machine access from the spawn area, iron pickup into a full/partial backpack, and all five upgrade outputs.
3. Check `git status` and review diffs, taking care not to overwrite user changes in `capture.mjs` or `capture.sh`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Game state, machine, iron, upgrades, interactions, and generated audio.
- `index.html`: HUD, hotbar, machine panel, and audio controls.
